final_text:
## Incident Report: STRRAT RAT Infection

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 585.66 sec capture, 2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34 UTC). No IDS/alert export was present in the evidence directory — only the pcap.

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 | Source of all suspicious traffic; sole non-DC/non-external host on the /24 |
| MAC | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 | Ethernet source on every frame with `ip.src==172.16.1.66` |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F | NBNS name registration (`<00>`/`<20>`) from 172.16.1.66; Kerberos `CNameString` = `desktop-skbr25f$`; confirmed again inside the STRRAT beacon payload |
| Domain | WIRESHARKWORKSHOP.ONLINE (DC 172.16.1.4, WIRESHARK-WS-DC) | DNS SRV/A records, Kerberos realm, LDAP/DRSUAPI/SAMR traffic between 172.16.1.66 and 172.16.1.4 |
| Logged-in user | ccollier | Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString=ccollier` at t=23.55s; matches the username field carried in every STRRAT beacon (`...DESKTOP-SKBR25F\|ccollier\|...`) |

### Malware family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT), version **1.6**. **Signature-confirmed** — not a guess. The infected host establishes a raw TCP session (stream 83) to the C2 and sends a plaintext, pipe-delimited beacon every ~5 seconds whose literal content is the STRRAT protocol signature:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|1 Sec
```

The `STRRAT` string, the pipe-delimited field layout (bot ID, hostname, username, OS, AV product, version, country, install status, uptime), and the length-prefixed frame (`"136\r\n\r\n"` before each ping) are the well-documented STRRAT check-in format. The bot ID `1BE8292C` and uptime counter increment on every beacon (`1 Sec` → `5 min 10 sec` at capture end), and the active-window field later populates with base64 `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` = `Program Manager`, another STRRAT beacon field. No commands were observed returning from the C2 in this capture window (server-to-client payload was empty on every turn — plain TCP ACKs only).

### Traffic shape / how it was found
Protocol hierarchy is dominated by normal AD/Windows/Office/Microsoft telemetry (LDAP, Kerberos, DCE-RPC, SMB2, TLS to Microsoft/Bing/MSN/Office CDNs). One conversation stands out: `172.16.1.66 <-> 141.98.10.79`, 411 frames, TCP port **49754 → 12132**, spanning 508 of the capture's 585 seconds, contacted directly by **bare IP with no preceding DNS lookup** for that address anywhere in the capture — the classic C2 shape the workflow calls out.

### Delivery-chain observation (behavioral, not confirmed)
Immediately before the first STRRAT beacon (t=76.99s), the host pulled two large TLS sessions:
- t≈64.2–64.9s: `github.com` (140.82.113.3) then `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133/109/111/108) — 653 frames / 833 KB
- t≈68.0s: `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) — 6,540 frames / 8.9 MB, largest conversation in the capture

Both present legitimate certificates (GitHub cert chain via DigiCert for `*.github.io`; GlobalSign cert for `repo1.maven.org`), so these are **not malicious infrastructure** — they are legitimate services being used to stage a payload, consistent with known STRRAT droppers that fetch a portable JRE and the RAT jar from legitimate hosts before launching. Because the sessions are TLS-encrypted, the exact object path/filename/hash cannot be recovered from this capture. This is reported as delivery-chain **context**, not a grounded IOC.

At t≈78.0s, the host also queried `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1) over plaintext HTTP and received a JSON geolocation response (`countryCode: US`) — this matches the `US:United States` field carried in the STRRAT beacon and is consistent with the RAT self-fingerprinting the victim's location on startup, seconds before the first beacon.

### IOCs

```json
{
  "victim": {
    "ip": "172.16.1.66",
    "mac": "00:1e:64:ec:f3:08",
    "hostname": "DESKTOP-SKBR25F",
    "user": "ccollier"
  },
  "malware_family": "STRRAT",
  "attribution_confidence": "signature-confirmed",
  "iocs": [
    {
      "type": "c2_endpoint",
      "value": "141.98.10.79:12132",
      "evidence": "TCP stream 83 (49754->12132), 508s duration, plaintext STRRAT 'ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|...' beacons every ~5s, no preceding DNS resolution for the IP"
    }
  ],
  "benign_context": [
    {"note": "repo1.maven.org (199.232.196.209/192.209) - legitimate Maven Central, GlobalSign cert, large TLS download at t=68s just before first beacon; possible JRE/jar staging but content not recoverable (encrypted)"},
    {"note": "github.com / objects.githubusercontent.com (140.82.113.3, 185.199.108-111.133) - legitimate GitHub, DigiCert cert, TLS download at t=64s, same timing pattern as above"},
    {"note": "ip-api.com (208.95.112.1) - legitimate geolocation API, plaintext HTTP GET /json/ at t=78s, response matches country field later seen in STRRAT beacon"},
    {"note": "172.16.1.4 (WIRESHARK-WS-DC.wiresharkworkshop.online) - domain controller, normal LDAP/Kerberos/DRSUAPI/SAMR traffic with victim"},
    {"note": "Microsoft/Bing/MSN/Office/WNS/OneDrive TLS traffic (23.x, 20.x, 52.x, 13.x address ranges) - standard Windows 11 / Office telemetry background noise"}
  ],
  "incident_summary": "Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user ccollier on WIRESHARKWORKSHOP.ONLINE, was infected with the STRRAT v1.6 Java RAT. Shortly after TLS sessions to GitHub and Maven Central (likely payload/JRE staging, content unrecoverable from ciphertext) and a geolocation lookup to ip-api.com, the host began beaconing every 5 seconds in plaintext to C2 141.98.10.79:12132 for the remainder of the capture, with no C2 commands observed returning in this window."
}
```

**No file name or SHA256 hash could be grounded** — the only sizeable transfers (GitHub, Maven Central) were TLS-encrypted with no HTTP object export available in this capture, so no artifact could be extracted or hashed.
